From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: leadership-distro@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Weekly exec digest — OKR status & QBR package request

Team,

Attached is a lightweight pack for this week’s exec pass — QBR prep + current OKR checkpoints. TL;DR: we’re generally on track but there are two notable risks that need prompt mitigation. Please review and add any items you want captured in the final QBR deck by Thursday EOD.

Wins
- Hosted API latency SLOs improved: p95 down 18% month-over-month after kernel tuning.
- Redwood Dedicated pilot passed initial throughput tests with ACME (see notes on slide 3).

Risks
- Edge case for long-context LLMs: memory pressure under burst load could push spooler fallback earlier than expected (impact: potential tail latency spikes on peak).
- Sales/legal cadence for ACME procurement: master terms need one more pass (legal flagged a data-retention clause).

Asks
- Markus: please attach the latency/time-to-first-token charts (p50/p95) and a one-line mitigation plan for the long-context memory issue.
- Laura: confirm renewal ARR numbers and whether we can offer a 60-day invoice net for ACME procurement (legal/finance alignment).
- Aditya: update the OKR metrics tab with current embedding unit consumption (sheet attached).

Attachments: QBR-Deck-V1.pdf, OKR-Metrics-Sheet.xlsx

I’ll consolidate updates on Wednesday and circulate a V2 deck ahead of Friday’s leadership review.

Thanks,

--
Lauren Bishop
VP, Product
Redwood Inference

Thanks, Lauren — solid summary. A couple quick points:

- I’ll add the latency charts today (p50/p95/TTF) and include a short note on the mitigation approach (KV cache tuning + staged rollout of the new allocator).
- The memory-pressure behavior you called out looks like it correlates with very long-context requests from the ACME pilot (they’re testing 80k token traces). We should propose a temporary rate-limit on sequences >32k until we have a safe allocator rollout.

Action: I’ll upload charts to the Drive and flag the slide that needs the wording tweak.

Thanks for kicking this off, Lauren. Quick updates from GTM/legal:

- Renewal ARR: conservative renewal number for ACME is $1.2M (pending final procurement signal). I’ve attached the finance snapshot to the shared folder.
- Billing/terms: Legal is pushing back on the open retention language; they want a clarified data lifecycle and an SLA for deletion. Procurement asked if we can do 90 days of invoice net instead of 60 — I suggested we hold to standard 30/60 tiers but can escalate if needed.

Also — for the QBR: can we add a single slide that calls out the production incident post-mortem template and our 30/60/90 remediation milestones? Customers like the clarity.

Laura

Folks — thank you for the quick turn. Final notes before I lock the deck: 

- Markus: I see the Drive upload (latency deck). Great — please add the exact mitigation bullet under Risks (I copied it to slide 5).
- Laura: noted on ARR and legal asks — I’ll add the 30/60/90 remediation slide and flag the retention question for the legal call on Thursday.
- Aditya: please push an updated OKR-Metrics-Sheet with the embedding consumption and the month-to-date cost delta by tomorrow morning.

I attached QBR-Deck-V2.pdf (consolidated) to this thread. Final ask: if you have any one-line wins you want surfaced in the exec brief, reply-all with them by 12:00 PM PST tomorrow. I’ll route the final deck to the broader leadership list on Friday morning.

Best,
